_readme: SYNTHETIC, HAND-BUILT LABELED CORPUS. This is not real bank data and
the accuracy numbers it produces are NOT real-world accuracy numbers.
Why it exists: the SimpleFIN demo server emits 3 distinct descriptions
across 338 transactions, with incoherent labels (fishing bait carrying
MCC 5812, Eating Places). Any accuracy measured on it is degenerate --
tier 1 reaches 100% after three confirmations and 'beats the
majority-class baseline' passes vacuously. See PLAN.md 3.1 and the
Phase 3 handoff.
What it measures: the MECHANICS of the cascade -- that the tiers fire
in the right order, that the memory tier generalizes across bank
manglings of the same merchant, that MCC is or is not separable, that
confidence ordering means something. It bounds the implementation, not
the product. Real accuracy is a Phase 6 question against real bank data.
How it was built: merchant surface forms were hand-authored to match
the bank-mangling shapes PLAN.md 3.1 names (SQ *..., TST* ..., ACH
DEBIT - ..., POS DEBIT ... #nnnn, AMZN Mktp US*...), then expanded into
dated instances by a seeded RNG. Labels are drawn only from the chart
of accounts in ledger/accounts.beancount.
Deliberate difficulty:
- the same merchant under several manglings and store numbers
- SAFEWAY (groceries) vs SAFEWAY FUEL (gas), COSTCO WHSE vs COSTCO GAS
- MCC 4900 shared by electric and water; MCC 4899 shared by internet
and Netflix -- the MCC tier provably cannot separate these
- WALGREENS and AMZN Mktp carry two different true labels, an
irreducible error floor no tier can beat
- CHECK #nnnn for rent: the number changes every time, so exact
memory can never match one
- entries flagged 'holdout' are novel one-off merchants pinned to the
test split; tiers 1-3 have never seen them by construction
- roughly two thirds of entries carry no payee and a third no MCC
